# strata

strata {{STRATA_VERSION}} renders infrastructure (Terraform, Helm, Compose, Ansible) from YAML documents. The
solution root holds `strata.yaml`; every other document is found by walking the tree below it. `.strata/` is
generated by strata and is never edited by hand.

## Ground rules

- Run `strata validate` after every document change; it must report no errors. Use `--strict` in CI so warnings
  fail too.
- Ask strata, do not guess: add `--output json` to any command for one machine-readable envelope
  (`ok`, `summary`, `diagnostics[]`, `data`).
- Never run `strata values get` to inspect configuration: it prints secrets in clear text. Use `values list` or
  `values resolve`, which never reveal a value.
- `build run` and the read-only commands are safe to run. Anything under `deploy` changes or plans real
  infrastructure, and `values set`/`values rotate` write to secret stores: only run those when the user asks.

## Commands

Exit codes: 0 success, 1 system failure, 2 usage error, 3 validation failure (the JSON envelope is still printed).

| Command | Use |
| --- | --- |
| `strata validate [PATH]` | Validate every document in the solution. |
| `strata graph [PATH]` | Every cross-document reference, resolved or not. |
| `strata path get KIND NAME` / `strata path list KIND` | Find a document's real file. |
| `strata deployment list` | Every deployment with the workspace and environments it resolves to (through `extends`); partial bases are marked. |
| `strata build run DEPLOYMENT` | Render a deployment into `build/` (never executes anything). `--dry-run` reports only. |
| `strata deploy setup / check / plan / apply / run DEPLOYMENT` | init, validate, plan, apply a saved plan, or all of it. |
| `strata values list / resolve / status DEPLOYMENT` | Inspect variables, secrets and features without revealing values. |
| `strata values get DEPLOYMENT KEY...` | Full values, secrets included. Not for inspection. |
| `strata values set / rotate / generate / mask` | Write or generate secret values. |
| `strata version new / set / update NAME` | Manage `kind: version` pin documents. |
| `strata promote status / view / apply WORKSPACE` | Ring/order/wave rollout of version documents. |
| `strata audit status / changes [DEPLOYMENT]` | Read back the deployment audit trail. |
| `strata policy list / check / findings DEPLOYMENT` | List the workspace's policies, evaluate them now (`cve_policy`, `checkov_policy`, the deploy gates), or list a policy's findings (all but `release_gate_policy`). |
| `strata integration check NAME` | Is an integration ready: enabled, tool on PATH, right version, and (where supported) credentials accepted. NAME is a document or a type; `--deployment` resolves credentials. |
| `strata integration list [--deployment D]` | Every integration's local readiness; with `--deployment`, what it is used for, failing when a used one is not ready. Offline. |
| `strata sln init NAME` / `strata sln update` | Create or refresh the scaffold files, including this skill. |

Run `strata <command> --help` for the full option list. A deployment is always named positionally
(`strata build run prd-c0062`); there is no `-f`/`--file`.

## Documents

Every document has `apiVersion`, `kind`, `meta.name` and `spec`. Documents reference each other by
`(kind, meta.name)`, never by file path. Exact fields for each kind are in `.strata/schemas/<kind>.json`.

Kinds: {{KINDS}}.

How values merge for a deployment:

- `variables`, `secrets` and `features` merge by `key`: a later environment replaces the whole entry. An object
  value is not deep-merged.
- `properties` and `custom` deep-merge: workspace, then environments, then the deployment.
- The tenant's environments merge before the deployment's own.

## Known pitfalls

- A key declared in both `properties` and `variables` anywhere in one deployment's merge chain is an error.
- `${...}` anywhere in a document, descriptions included, is read as a strata value token. Write `$${...}` for a
  literal, for example another tool's own syntax.
- Terraform receives one `strata` object (`strata.auto.tfvars.json`). A root reads `local.strata.*`; it does not get
  one flat variable per key.
- A Helm module's `configuration` becomes the chart's `values.yaml`. It replaces the chart's own values, it is not
  merged on top of them.
- `deploy run --dry-run` runs a real `init`/`validate`/`plan`: it needs credentials and takes the state lock.
- `deploy run --force` has no effect.
- A remote with `fetch: external` must already be checked out at `.strata/remotes/<name>/<reference>` before
  `build run`; strata will not clone it.
- A version pin on a `type: local` remote is accepted but changes nothing.
- An `attributeconfig` must set `target.view` (`document` or `effective`); there is no default.

Project-specific lessons belong in the `project-gotchas` skill, not here: this file is rewritten on every
`strata sln update`.
